name: auth_log
description: Parse auth.log or secure, including the rotated and gzipped files, into one record per line with fields and locators: ssh acceptances (method, user, source, port, key type and fingerprint, and a certificate's id, serial and CA), failures (a rejected public key's type and fingerprint included), invalid users and disconnects (the source is an address or it is not a source), sudo and su lines (the working directory and target user), PAM failures read as key=value pairs, PAM sessions with the service they belong to, `Accepted key` lines (kind key_observed_authentication: sshd matched a login to an authorized_keys entry, not a key being installed), account changes. Reads the files oldest first by their rotation suffix and says which basis ordered each. A traditional syslog stamp has no year and no zone: each record keeps the stamp as written (time_raw), the year applied (from the file's modification time or your year argument, said per file) and time_zone unknown; a month that steps back is read as a year end only within six months forward, and otherwise as a reordered line; a line the next line contradicts is a stray (reordered) and does not date the file; the last line in order, with a day's margin for the unknown zone, dates it. The year is an inference, and the answer says how weak it is: a month that goes up keeps the same year however long the gap, so each file lists in forward_steps every step of more than 62 days between two consecutive lines in order (line, from_line, from, to, days; the first 20 inline, all of them in pages.forward_steps), and every record with a traditional stamp before the last such step carries year_assumed: true, because any number of years may have passed across it; year_anchor names the last line in order and the modification time that dated it; mtime_may_be_copy_time is true, with its reasons in mtime_may_be_copy_time_why, when that time is more than 7 days after the last dated line, when every file of a call of more than one has the same modification time to within 10 seconds, or when a gzip file's header time (gzip_header_time, the MTIME of RFC 1952, none when 0; gzip_header_agrees_with_modified, to within 2 seconds) differs from it, because then the year is the year of a copy. The dating rule and the status are unchanged: fix the year from a source with full dates and pass year (every file) or years (a year for a file from a line on) before a conclusion rests on a date, and a record dated by your year is not year_assumed. An RFC 3339 stamp keeps its own offset and fractions (`time` is the clock reading as written, `time_utc` the same instant in UTC only where the stamp carries its zone). A line longer than 64 KiB is located and not parsed, a long free-text field is shown cut with its whole length (the whole is in the text file), only gzip is read (another compression is a named read error), and a pipe or device is never opened. Every record carries its file, physical line and byte offset; a line no rule places, a gzip cut off mid-stream and a file that could not be read are counted and located, and all_lines_parsed is true only when none happened. It is a line reader, not an account of the host's authentication events: it does not read the journal, wtmp or the audit log, and a fingerprint names a key, not a person. SENSITIVE: a sudo line is a command line, and a name typed at a prompt can be a password. It is withheld by its position in a line the tool recognises, never by what it looks like: the name of an `Invalid user` or `Illegal user` line (everything up to the last `from <address>`, spaces included), of a failure for an invalid or illegal user, of a disconnect from an invalid user (where the line is not sshd's form `<name> <address> port <n>` with at most a bracketed stage, the whole of what follows the words is the name and no source is read), and a PAM `user=` (the rest of the line) or `ruser=`. The answer never carries `raw`, a `command` or such a name, only their lengths (user_bytes, user_withheld); a line the tool does not recognise is `other` and prints no field. A name the log accepted, or that a session, sudo or su line names, stays in the answer. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/auth-text.jsonl, mode 0600, with the text of every record and unparsed line (the typed names included), and preview_text: true (refused outside a job) puts it in the answer; run it as a job with secret_output: true. max_seconds (default 100, at most 105) bounds the walk of a directory and the read (it is read between lines and inside a line of many megabytes): a file it did not reach is named under files_not_reached. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP ends the tool with one JSON last word (status failed, exit 128 plus the signal) naming the paging files and the text file it had written; the handlers are installed from the first line after the imports, so only the interpreter's own start-up is outside them. A paging or text write that fails (a full disk) keeps the rows already written under the file's name, or removes its temporary, and the error answer says which. The text file holds at most 256 MiB: past it the records are counted (`not_written` in `text`), the answer is partial and the rest is in the evidence at the locators; the paging files hold at most 128 MiB together, with the same `not_written` in `pages`. Lists that grow with the evidence keep their first 200 items inline and the whole of each in a paging file named in pages.<list> (files, files_not_reached, read_errors, walk_errors, skipped_symlinks, skipped_special and cross_file_order_overlaps; a list with nothing in it has no page); the clock is read for every file and every 256 directory entries, so a directory of many files, or a whole file system, ends at max_seconds as partial. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries: all_lines_parsed stays beside it, true only when no line went unplaced or unread. A disk image (E01, raw, VHD(X), VMDK, QCOW2, by its first bytes, or by its name and a boot sector) is refused with the routes that read one: the catalogue's linux-target files, linux_triage, or files extracted first in a job with target-fs.

path.description: An auth.log or secure file, or a directory of them (rotated files are found and read oldest first; links are not followed and are listed)

kinds.description: Keep only these kinds, e.g. ["ssh_accepted","sudo"]. Known: ssh_accepted, ssh_failed, ssh_invalid_user, ssh_disconnect, key_observed_authentication, sudo, sudo_failed, su, session_opened, session_closed, auth_failure, account_added, account_changed, other

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring over the fields the answer shows; in a job, over the whole line, including the text the answer withholds (the answer then says filter_touched_withheld_text). It filters what is returned, never what is counted as parsed

year.description: The year (1970 to 2200) to apply to every traditional syslog line of every file that a years range does not cover. Without it each file's year is assumed from its modification time and the months' own year ends (see forward_steps, year_assumed, year_anchor and mtime_may_be_copy_time in the answer); with it a file that crosses a year end says year_argument_spans_rollover

years.description: A year per file and per line range, for a file that spans years: [{"file": <a path as the answer's files[].path gives it>, "from_line": <physical line, 1 or more>, "year": <1970 to 2200>}]. Each entry applies its year to every traditional line from from_line to the next entry of the same file (or the end), unchanged across a year end (years_span_rollover says when a range holds one); the entries of a file must ascend by from_line and may not repeat one, each file must be one of the call's, at most 1000 entries, and anything else is refused before anything is read. It is applied before the year assumed from the modification time, and before year; year_basis and years_applied say where it applied

max_expanded_bytes.description: How far a gzip stream is read once decompressed (default 1073741824); past it the file ends as a read error and the answer is partial

limit.description: Records and unparsed lines shown inline (default 200 each); all of them are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

write_text.description: SENSITIVE: Write the text of every record (raw, a sudo command, the physical line) to $OUT/auth-text.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused; the answer never carries the text (declared secret_output: a job that sets write_text is run as secret output, and the tool refuses write_text when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1)

preview_text.description: SENSITIVE: Put raw and a sudo command in the answer's records (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true (declared secret_output: a job that sets preview_text is run as secret output, and the tool refuses preview_text when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1)

max_seconds.description: The time to spend reading (default 100, at most 105); a file it did not reach is named and the answer is partial
